title: Course Order
statement:
Find an order in which all courses can be taken so that every prerequisite comes before the course that needs it.

Contract
- Courses are numbered `0` to `courses - 1`. Each pair `{course, prerequisite}` in `prerequisites` means `prerequisite` must be taken somewhere before `course`.
- Return an array containing every course exactly once in a valid order. When several orders work, any one of them is accepted.
- If the prerequisites cannot all be satisfied (for example they form a cycle, including a course that requires itself), return an empty array.
- `courses` may be 0, `prerequisites` may be empty, and the same pair may appear more than once. Do not modify the input.

Examples
- `courseOrder(4, new int[][]{{1,0},{2,1},{3,2}})` returns `[0, 1, 2, 3]`.
- `courseOrder(3, new int[][]{{0,1},{1,2},{2,0}})` returns an empty array because the courses wait on each other in a loop.
- `courseOrder(3, new int[0][])` returns the three courses in any order, such as `[0, 1, 2]`.
hints: A course can be taken as soon as everything it depends on has been taken, so start with the courses that need nothing.
Count how many unmet prerequisites each course has. Repeatedly take a course with count zero, and lower the count of every course that was waiting on it.

If you manage to take fewer courses than exist, the rest are stuck in a cycle, so return an empty array. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(n) space, where n is the number of courses plus the number of prerequisite pairs.
inputSyntax: Input: the course count, then the [course, prerequisite] pairs, for example: 4 [[1, 0], [2, 1], [3, 2]]
